body:
## Finding

The Harness has Jev claim-support evaluation, but this audit found no end-to-end workflow that resolves scholarly citation identities and records which primary-source passage supports each report claim. A live literature review can therefore have a research plan and relevant web hits while still containing a wrong DOI/title/year, a preprint/journal mismatch, or a citation that does not support the attached claim. This is separate from the shared research-plan/result lifecycle in #342 and per-result relevance in #343.

## Deterministic end state

Each report claim and bibliography item has a stable ID and a provenance record. Bibliography metadata is resolved from an authoritative DOI/metadata registry or publisher page and compared with the supplied title, authors, year, venue, DOI, and version. Each factual claim links to one or more retrieved source records and an exact passage locator (page, section, paragraph, or stable URL anchor), with source type and retrieval timestamp recorded.

The system assigns only closed-set statuses: supported, partially_supported, contradicted, or not_verifiable. Metadata mismatch, unavailable source, paywall, retrieval failure, missing passage, or version ambiguity cannot be silently promoted to verified. Jev may advise on semantic support; code-owned checks decide metadata matches, provenance completeness, and whether a report may be labeled citation-verified. No generated citation metadata is invented.

## Acceptance criteria

- DOI resolution records the canonical DOI and metadata source/version used; supplied metadata mismatches are surfaced field by field.
- DOI-less and non-journal sources can be recorded honestly with their actual source class and stable URL; unavailable metadata remains unknown.
- Claim-to-source records preserve exact retrieved passage text or a hash-pinned bounded excerpt plus locator, source URL/DOI, source class, and retrieval time.
- Tests cover exact match, wrong DOI, title/author/year mismatch, preprint vs. published version, partial support, contradiction, no supporting passage, inaccessible/paywalled source, HTTP/rate-limit failure, and conflicting registry/publisher metadata.
- A report cannot claim citation verification when required metadata or claim evidence is missing; the output shows unresolved items and retains honest-insufficiency behavior.
- The implementation integrates with #342's accepted research lifecycle and preserves request-bound evidence from #344; existing source relevance remains governed by #343.

## Canonical research-plan dependency (2026-10-28)

The operational acquisition and result lifecycle is defined in [`docs/jev-roadmap.md`](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/blob/main/docs/jev-roadmap.md) and implemented through #342–#344: accepted, query-bound retrieval proposal; per-candidate and final-destination validation; and request-bound checkpoint/evidence freshness. This issue owns the later citation-identity and claim-to-passage audit, not initial query authorization or relevance filtering.

Only retrieved source records that pass that lifecycle may enter citation verification. Preserve the exact source version, locator, retrieval time and bounded passage/hash; a search result snippet, quoted trace, or unreviewed citation string is not claim evidence. Unresolved metadata or support remains unresolved in the final report.


---

<!-- canonical-plan-sync:pr-431 -->
### Canonical cross-issue plan (2026-10-28)
The shared execution order, dependencies, research/retrieval policy, and system-wide acceptance matrix are maintained in the [canonical roadmap PR #431](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/pull/431) (docs/jev-roadmap.md, “Canonical reconciliation and verified web-research plan”). This issue remains the scoped acceptance contract for 422; keep its deliverable and issue-specific evidence here, and update the roadmap when a cross-issue dependency, ordering rule, or shared gate changes. Do not maintain a parallel plan or file a duplicate issue for the same finding.

<!-- jev-lead-verification-2026-10-28 -->

## 2026-10-28 follow-up verification

**Disposition: production capability gap confirmed by targeted source inspection.** The current production citation/search/render paths have no DOI resolver, Crossref/OpenAlex metadata lookup, field-by-field bibliography check, or exact-passage locator. `evaluate_claim_support` is an optional Jev check and does not provide deterministic citation identity/provenance verification. Targeted repository search found no metadata-registry integration in those paths. No external bibliography was verified in this audit continuation.

## Selected science-review claim audit — 2026-10-28

This continuation produced [reports/ai-for-science-review-2026-10.md](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/blob/freebuff/audit-this-harness-request-in-full-331d44a9-d477-4530-924b-ce019bc59e3d/reports/ai-for-science-review-2026-10.md), a selected review draft with manually checked primary-source claim relationships. This supersedes the earlier follow-up sentence that no external bibliography was verified. The review corrects the GraphCast horizon/resolution claim, FunSearch lower-bound attribution, tokamak simulator-to-device training description, GNoME/A-Lab dataset and synthesis denominator conflation, and RFdiffusion/backbone versus sequence-design distinction. It labels the 2026 AlphaProof Nexus work as a preprint and does not claim exhaustive or publication-ready status.

This was a manual review of cited primary records, not an automated DOI-registry resolution or complete field-by-field bibliography audit. The Harness still lacks stable citation IDs, authoritative metadata comparison, exact passage locators, and deterministic claim-support status. Keep those implementation gaps and acceptance tests open under this issue; the report and its links are not a substitute for the product capability.

2026-10-28 follow-up from PR #431.

The selected 2020 to 2026 science review draft is available in reports/ai-for-science-review-2026-10.md. It corrects material overclaims and distinguishes predictions from independent validation. It is a manually checked draft, not an automated DOI/passage audit, peer-reviewed paper, exhaustive review, or publication-ready manuscript.

The canonical plan now specifies a claim ledger with source/version identity, DOI resolution outcome, exact passage locator, claim-to-source support state, check date and reviewer/tool provenance. Unsupported or unresolved claims remain unverified. Please retain this issue as the implementation owner for metadata identity and exact-passage verification; the report itself does not close it.

title: [research] Verify citation metadata and claim-to-source support
